definition: critical explanation or analysis of a text
example: His exegesis of the poem won academic acclaim.

definition: to absolve from blame or responsibility
example: New evidence exonerated the suspect.

definition: treating serious issues with inappropriate humor
example: Her facetious remarks undermined the meeting.

definition: foolishness; something foolish
example: His fatuity in business cost the firm millions.

definition: conspicuously or obviously offensive
example: The flagrant misconduct led to her dismissal.

definition: to deny or contradict
example: There's no gainsaying his contribution to the field.

definition: an act or remark designed to gain an advantage
example: Her opening gambit was a brilliant concession.

definition: relevant to the subject at hand
example: Please keep your comments germane to the topic.

definition: a person or thing that announces or signals the approach of another
example: The early frost was a harbinger of a hard winter.

definition: simple and unsophisticated; homemade in style
example: Her homespun wisdom charmed the city audience.

definition: of, based on, or serving as a hypothesis; supposed
example: She posed a hypothetical question about the future.

definition: not honorable in character or purpose
example: He was driven by ignoble motives.

definition: a complicated or confusing situation
example: The diplomatic imbroglio dragged on for months.

definition: impossible to imitate or copy
example: Her inimitable voice won her a global audience.

definition: a period of time between two successive reigns or governments
example: The country endured a long interregnum before the new ruler arrived.

definition: to abandon or discard someone or something
example: The company jettisoned its troubled subsidiary.

definition: having or showing good judgment
example: A judicious editor improves every manuscript.

definition: tearful or given to weeping
example: The lachrymose protagonist mourned all night.

definition: generosity in bestowing money or gifts
example: The donor's largesse funded an entire library wing.

definition: more merciful or tolerant than expected
example: The judge was known for her lenient sentences.

definition: looking or sounding sad and dismal
example: The lugubrious music fit the rainy afternoon.

definition: a plot or scheme, especially to do harm
example: His rivals uncovered the machination just in time.

definition: easily influenced; pliable
example: Young minds are malleable and open to new ideas.

definition: lacking in quantity or quality; deficient
example: They survived on a meager diet of rice and fish.

definition: the lowest or most unsuccessful point
example: The team's nadir came after the ten-game losing streak.
